findings.title: `.contents .title { float: left; }` removed with no flex replacement
findings.body: The diff removes the `.title { float: left; }` rule that previously positioned the site title/logo text inside `.d-header .contents`, while simultaneously turning `.contents` into a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). No equivalent flex property (e.g. flex-basis, flex-shrink, min-width) was added for `.title`. Since `.title` becomes an un-constrained flex item, its sizing/wrapping behavior changes from the previous float-based layout with no verification that the new default flex-item behavior produces the same visual result, especially now that `.panel` is pushed to the far right via `margin-left: auto`. This risks the header title overlapping or being squeezed incorrectly on narrow viewports.

findings.title: Leftover float-era margin-top conflicts with new flex align-items:center
findings.body: `.login-button, button.sign-up-button` still use `float: left; margin-top: 7px;` (lines 42-47), which was presumably hand-tuned to vertically align the buttons when the header items were float-based. Now that the parent `.contents` is a flex container with `align-items: center` (lines 17-18), floats are ignored on flex items and the leftover `margin-top: 7px` will simply add extra space inside the already vertically-centered flex item, pushing the login/sign-up buttons lower than the other centered header elements (logo, icons, panel). This was not reconciled as part of the flexbox migration.

findings.title: Removed `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` alignment fix without replacement
findings.body: The previous `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` rule provided a vertical-alignment correction specifically for the bullet-style category badge. This diff deletes that nested rule and replaces it only with `@include order(2); line-height: 1.5;` at the `.extra-info-wrapper` level, which does not address the same bullet-specific offset. This removes a previously necessary alignment fix without any compensating change, risking visual misalignment of bullet category badges in topic titles/suggested topics.

findings.title: `order()` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` without confirmed flex parent
findings.body: `@include order(2);` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but the CSS `order` property only has an effect when the element's direct parent is a flex (or grid) container. Nothing in this file (or the diff) establishes that the actual DOM parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` has `display: flex` set. If the parent is not a flex container, this change is a no-op, meaning the ordering intent of the change may silently fail without any indication in the PR of where/if the parent flex context exists.

findings.title: Undocumented spacing changes to `.small-action-desc` bundled into a 'header flexbox' PR
findings.body: Beyond adding `@include flexbox()`/`@include align-items(center)` to `.small-action`, the diff also changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, drops its `margin-top: 5px`, changes `.custom-message p` margin from `5px 0` to `0`, and removes `> p { padding-top: 4px; }`. None of these spacing changes are explained in the PR description (which is just 'Test 5'), and they are unrelated to the stated purpose of optimizing header layout. These values directly affect spacing of topic timeline 'small action' notices (e.g. pinned/closed messages) and risk unintended overlap or cramped spacing between the avatar icon and description text, with no visual regression verification included.

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimization but changes are a layout/mixin refactor
findings.body: The PR title states 'Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins', but the actual diff only introduces reusable flexbox mixins and swaps float-based layout for flexbox in several unrelated stylesheets (header, topic, topic-post, badges). There is no measurement, benchmark, or explanation showing any performance improvement; flexbox vs. float is not inherently a performance optimization for this static layout. Combined with the empty description ('Test 5'), this makes the rationale and scope of the change unclear to reviewers and future maintainers, especially given the changes span files unrelated to the header.
